stem_book: [One or more than one option may be correct] If concentration of two weak acids are different and D.O.I. (α) are very less then their relative strength can be compared by: (a) [H⁺]₁/[H⁺]₂ (b) α₁/α₂ (c) C₁α₁/C₂α₂ (d) √(K_a1·C₁/K_a2·C₂)
key: (a), (c), (d) all except (b), which needs equal concentrations
reason: Coordinator: printed option missing a root sign; correction unconfirmed - not used. Print drops the √ in (d) (shows K_a1C₁/K_a2C₂, which is the SQUARE of the strength ratio); restored from the lecture's own √(K_a1/K_a2) strength relation, the manifest transcription and the standard form of this question.
work: Strength ratio = [H⁺]₁/[H⁺]₂ = C₁α₁/C₂α₂ = √(K_a1C₁)/√(K_a2C₂); α₁/α₂ = √(K_a1C₂/K_a2C₁) ≠ ratio unless C₁ = C₂
